newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq in big new wheat deal with France.
newsitem.headline: Iraq in big new wheat deal with France.

text.p: Iraq has finalised contracts to buy wheat from France worth almost $50 million under the oil-for-food deal it struck with the United Nations last year, European grain traders said on Wednesday.
Contracts covered between 250,000 and 275,000 tonnes of French wheat for March and April delivery at prices between $184 and $185 per tonne, the traders said.
The price includes the cost of shipping, they said.
Iraq is buying grain now that the United Nations has eased its Gulf War embargo on its oil exports under an accord that lets it use the money to buy food and medicine.
French companies have also sold 50,000 tonnes of sugar to Iraq in the past few days but the value of that deal is unknown, a French budget ministry official said.
The grain purchase is a major relief for French firms which have been worrying for the past week that a potential rift between Paris and Baghdad could scupper the deal.

Iraq's official media criticised Paris last week for refusing to allow Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's son, Uday, wounded in an assassination attempt last month, to be treated in France, though Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz has indicated that this would not seriously damage relations.
France, which has lent conditional support to Baghdad's calls for a complete end to international sanctions, is expected to reap a number of oil and grain deals in return.
French food exporters said they were concerned, however, that strict U.N. monitoring of oil-for-food sales was holding up the delivery of wheat previously sold to Iraq in December.
Under the rules of the U.N. pact, all food and oil contracts must be passed to a special committee at the world body's headquarters for approval before shipments can be made.
France has applied for permission to ship around 200,000 tonnes of wheat sold to Iraq in December but so far nothing has been heard from the U.N. inspectors, traders said.
Iraq says wheat will make up more than half the two million tonnes of commodities it plans to buy with cash raised from crude oil exports which resumed in December.
France is a major supplier of the grain alongside Australia and Argentina, which are also selling to Iraq.
But the United States, Iraq's second supplier behind Australia before 1990, and its main Gulf War enemy, is seen unlikely to find favour, barring shortages elsewhere.
